I have been farming this 340 mu for 3 years now. Before that I worked in construction, but I came back to take over the family land and rented more from relatives. I finished middle school, and I have gone to two training sessions at the township ag station. I also talk a lot with the seed dealer in town and watch what my neighbor Old Wang does on his 200 mu.

This year I will keep 300 mu in the wheat-summer crop rotation because that is what works here in Quzhou. I plant the improved wheat variety that Old Wang uses — I think it is a Jimai type, I just ask the dealer for the same bags as last year. Last year I used 50 kg per mu of compound fertilizer as base, then top-dressed urea twice. I got about 500 kg per mu, which was okay but not great. This year I will push it a little: 55 kg compound fertilizer and 25 kg urea at green-up plus another 10 kg at jointing. That is about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu, 7 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium. I know it is a lot of money — fertilizer prices are high — but on 300 mu if I lose yield I am finished. I would rather spend an extra 50 yuan per mu on fertilizer than risk dropping 100 kg. I irrigate 4 times: before winter, at green-up, at jointing, and at heading. My well can handle it. I hire the machinery cooperative for rotary tillage before wheat planting, 50 yuan per mu. For chemicals, I spray herbicide once after planting and fungicide once at flowering.

For summer maize, I plant hybrid seed right after the wheat comes out in June on 280 mu. I use no-tillage direct seeding — you cannot waste time plowing in summer, the heat hits fast. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and side-dress urea at big-flare stage. Total is about 16 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, 6 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate 3 times: jointing, flowering, and grain filling. Two pesticide sprays, one for weeds and one for corn borer. Last year I got 600 kg per mu, this year I expect 600 kg per mu if the weather holds.

On 20 mu of the wheat ground I will plant summer soybean instead of maize. The soybean is an improved variety, low fertilizer because the roots fix nitrogen — about 3 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, 4 kg potassium. Two irrigations, two sprays. I expect 170 kg per mu.

The other 40.1 mu I keep for spring peanut. Peanut needs loose soil so I pay for ploughing, 80 yuan per mu. I put 8 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, 8 kg potassium because peanut eats a lot of potash. Three irrigations and three sprays — peanut gets disease if you are lazy. I expect 320 kg per mu.

With 340 mu and only 4 people in my house, I hire labor for spraying and harvesting. I spend about 40,000 yuan on fertilizer alone. It keeps me up at night. But I have learned that skimping on inputs is how you go broke. I watch my neighbors, and the ones who apply heavy fertilizer and irrigate on time are the ones still farming. The ones who cut corners are working in factories now. I will do what worked last year, just a little more.
